While the low population density of these areas lowers the likelihood of exposure and spread (less than 5 million people live on permafrost), communities living close to thawing sites may face increased risks, as animal carcasses or human remains are discovered. In Siberia for instance, in a particularly hot summer of 2016, 2,649 reindeers were killed and 36 people sickened by the Bacillus anthracis, the cause of anthrax.13 Scientists fear that it may have been released from the frozen ground.
